name: Image Type
abstract: ADA image with componentType classification for analytical images. Defines properties: @type, acquisitionTime, componentType, channel1, channel2, channel3, pixelSize, illuminationType, imageType.
description:
# Image Type

Describes image objects in ADA metadata with acquisition details and component type classification. Typed as `ada:image` and `schema:ImageObject`. Supports various analytical image types including EPMA, SEM, TEM, STEM, and spectroscopic images.

examples.title: Image Type Example
examples.content: An SEM backscattered electron image with component type and acquisition details.

$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema

    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/illuminationType

    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/imageType
  ada:spatialRegistration:
    title: Pixel Scaling
    description: 'Pixel size and its units. SCALING ONLY -- the half of a spatial
      registration an unregistered image can state. A plain image has a pixel size,
      and ada:pixelScaleX on an ada:EPMAImage is a well-formed statement, but an image
      does not say where it sits on the sample or how its axes relate to the sample
      axes. The imageMap block references the full shape, which adds the origin, the
      origin corner, the coordinate definition and the two rotation terms, and whose
      required list demands them.

      Same property NAME on both branches on purpose: a placement path such as schema:hasPart[@type=ada:image|ada:imageMap].ada:spatialRegistration.ada:pixelScaleX
      then resolves through either, which is what the subject-key register and the
      TAPP sidecars both target. Before this, the image branch declared no spatialRegistration
      at all -- not because a pixel scale is meaningless on an image, but because
      the only available shape required an origin and a corner, so an image could
      not use it without asserting a registration it does not have.'
    $ref: https://amds-ldeo.github.io/geochemBuildingBlocks/build/annotated/BaseSchema/spatialRegistration/schema.yaml#/$defs/Scaling
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/spatialRegistration
required:
- '@type'
- ada:componentType
$defs:
  PixelDimension:
    title: Pixel Dimension
    description: 'A raster dimension in pixels, as a schema:QuantitativeValue. ONE
      declaration, referenced by every block that needs it, so the shape cannot drift
      between them -- which it already had: geochemProduct declared schema:width as
      this object while a draft technique block declared it as anyOf[integer, string],
      and a value satisfying either violated the other. Nothing caught that, because
      the two blocks are validated separately.

      A QuantitativeValue rather than a bare integer, following the reason geochemProduct
      already records: the same schema.org property carries physical dimensions elsewhere,
      so the unit has to be stated rather than assumed to be pixels -- and schema:size
      beside it already takes this shape.

      schema:width and schema:height are used in preference to the ada: equivalents
      they replace (ada:numPixelsX, ada:numPixelsY), because a schema.org property
      that applies is preferred to a minted one.

      ada:pixelSize was listed here as a third replaced property, and that was wrong
      twice over. It is not a pixel COUNT, so schema:width and schema:height cannot
      express it -- the paragraph above is exactly why, since a property whose unit
      must be STATED rather than assumed cannot also be the property that states the
      count. What supersedes ada:pixelSize is the other axis entirely: ada:spatialRegistration.ada:pixelScaleX
      / ada:pixelScaleY with ada:pixelUnits, the SCALING half this block already references
      from spatialRegistration/$defs/Scaling, whose title is "Pixel Scaling" and whose
      description is "pixel size and its units". That form is the better one -- it
      separates the two axes, so an anisotropic pixel is sayable, and it carries the
      unit in a property of its own, which "0.5 micrometer" as one string does not.
      This block''s example has been migrated accordingly, to pixelScaleX/Y of 0.5
      with ada:pixelUnits "micrometer", and image/rules.shacl now asks for the scaling
      rather than for ada:pixelSize.

      The claim that came with it, "nothing is lost: no example carried the ada: forms",
      was false for every one of the three, and the examples have now been migrated
      so that it is true. Measured over examples.yaml and example*.json before the
      move: ada:pixelSize in image/examples.yaml, ada:numPixelsX/Y in imageMap/examples.yaml
      AND supDocImage/examples.yaml, against schema:width in only the three STEM detail
      examples. The counts were declared here in their schema.org form while two examples
      still wrote the ada: form, and they validated solely because neither block is
      sealed -- so nothing reported it. All three now carry the schema.org forms,
      and the three shapes ask for them: imageMap and supDocImage for schema:width
      / schema:height, this block for ada:spatialRegistration.'
    type: object
    properties:
      '@type':
        type: array
        items:
          type: string
        contains:
          const: schema:QuantitativeValue
        minItems: 1
      schema:value:
        type: number
        description: The dimension in pixels.
        x-jsonld-id: http://schema.org/value
      schema:unitText:
        type: string
        description: Unit of measure, e.g. 'pixel'.
        x-jsonld-id: http://schema.org/unitText
x-jsonld-prefixes:
  schema: http://schema.org/
  ada: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/
